sections.h2: Which Randolph County office sets and bills property tax?
sections.html:
The Randolph County Tax Department. Its website has separate pages for real property, rates, reappraisal, liens, the annual property tax scroll, relief applications and foreclosure sales, plus a tax bill lookup and a real property search.

Eleven municipalities appear on the county's rate page: Asheboro, Archdale, Franklinville, Liberty, Ramseur, Randleman, Seagrove, Staley, High Point, Thomasville and Trinity. Which charges reach your bill depends on whether the parcel lies in one of them and in which fire district.

sections.h2: What rates does Randolph County list for 2026-2027?
sections.html:
The county's rate page, headed 2026-2027, shows 0.50 as the county rate. It does not use the word adopted, so confirm the figures on your own bill with the tax department.

City rates, school rates and fire rates are listed on top of the county rate. The city list is below as the page prints it.

sections.h2: What school, fire and vehicle charges does Randolph County add?
sections.html:
Two school rates are printed: 0.1153 for Asheboro and 0.0803 for Trinity. Eighteen fire districts are on the list, with rates from 0.10 for Staley to 0.18 for Climax.

  • Fire rates include Fair Grove 0.132, Guil-Rand 0.15, Julian 0.135, Westside 0.16, Eastside 0.17, Level Cross 0.17 and Ulah 0.12.
  • More fire rates: Seagrove 0.12, Tabernacle 0.1225, Northeast (Liberty) 0.17, Rand Soph 0.17, Coleridge-Erect 0.12, Franklinville 0.16, Bennett 0.11, Farmer 0.12 and Southwest (New Hope) 0.12.
  • Flat vehicle fees: High Point 30.00, Liberty 5.00 and Thomasville 20.00.
  • Dog fees appear too: 5.00 in Randolph, 5.00 in Ramseur and 0.00 in Liberty.

A rural parcel pays the county rate plus a fire rate, and an in-town parcel adds its city rate. Ask the tax department to confirm your districts.

sections.h2: How do the layers stack up for an Asheboro address?
sections.html:
An in-town house in the Asheboro school area carries three printed layers on the county's 2026-2027 page: the county rate of 0.50, the Asheboro city rate of 0.71 and the Asheboro school rate of 0.1153. A fire rate can sit on top depending on the district, and the tax department can tell you whether yours does.

An address in Archdale, Franklinville or Seagrove draws on a different city figure, and a house outside every town skips the city layer entirely. That spread is why two Randolph County houses with the same assessed value can get different bills. When you list, tell a buyer which district you sit in, since the combined rate shapes the monthly payment on the buyer's loan.

sections.h2: How often does Randolph County revalue property?
sections.html:
Every four years, which is shorter than the state's eight-year minimum. The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2023, and the county's real property page says the next is scheduled for 2027.

A proposed 2027 schedule of values and a proposed present-use schedule are posted, so treat them as drafts until commissioners act. The county says its aim is full market value on every parcel. A 2027 revaluation year is when many sellers see the biggest swing in assessed value, so read the notice when it arrives.

sections.h2: How does the Randolph County Tax Department decide what a house is worth?
sections.html:
It studies sales in the county, records each property's size, construction, heating and cooling, plumbing, age and condition, and weighs the income a property could earn. Values do not move evenly: depending on recent sales in a market area, an assessment may rise, fall or stay about the same.

The reappraisal page also notes that the reappraisal sets only one half of the bill, the assessed value, while elected officials set the rate.

sections.h2: Why does the 2027 reappraisal matter to a Randolph County seller?
sections.html:
It resets the assessed value that a buyer's first full bill is built on. The county's page says properties do not change uniformly: a market area with strong recent sales may rise, another may fall or stay flat.

Under the county's explanation of state law, market value means the price both sides would accept without pressure. If your house is priced below what the county's appraisers see in nearby sales, expect a higher notice. If you have made repairs or additions, report them so the record matches.

  • Check your parcel in the county's real property search.
  • Read the reappraisal value notice as soon as it comes.
  • Use the informal appeal form mailed with the notice before moving to a board hearing.

sections.h2: Which reasons does the county accept to appeal in Randolph County?
sections.html:
Randolph lists two: an assessment far above market value, or one out of line with similar properties nearby. It lists as invalid that the value is simply too high, that taxes are high or that the owner cannot afford the bill.

The path runs through an informal appeal, mailed with each reappraisal notice, then Randolph's review board, the state commission that hears property tax cases and the appellate court. A commission appeal is due 30 days after the board mails its ruling, per G.S. 105-290. Ask the tax department for the board's meeting dates.

sections.h2: Who is billed if a Randolph County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever owned it on January 1. The county's real property page says the bill is always generated for that owner, and that commissioners adopted a permanent listing system, so land is listed automatically as soon as the register of deeds records a deed. Building changes still must be reported in the listing period.

Payment at face value is allowed through January 5, and the collection statute adds 2 percent interest from January 6 and 0.75 percent per month from February 1. Who shares which part of that year's bill is a closing negotiation.

sections.h2: Which relief and collection rules matter to a Randolph County seller?
sections.html:
Randolph posts a relief page and an application form. The state programs are the senior and disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment, and an owner can use only one. They sit in G.S. 105-277.1, G.S. 105-277.1C and G.S. 105-277.1B.

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien, and deferred tax for the three prior years comes due on a sale. If a bill stays unpaid, the county can foreclose through an action filed where the land lies, with a public auction at the courthouse door under G.S. 105-374. Selling first, even to a cash buyer, avoids that path.

sections.h2: When can Randolph County owners report building changes?
sections.html: January's first business day starts the state listing period, which closes January 31 under G.S. 105-307, with extensions available for good cause but not past April 15. Land is listed on its own in Randolph, so the window matters for added rooms, removed structures and business equipment.

faqs.q: What is Randolph County's reappraisal schedule?
faqs.a: A four-year cycle. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the county says the next is scheduled for 2027.

faqs.q: What county rate does Randolph County list for 2026-2027?
faqs.a: The county's page prints 0.50, with city, school and fire rates listed apart from it. Call the tax department to confirm your total.

faqs.q: Is high tax a valid reason to appeal a Randolph County value?
faqs.a: No. The county names high taxes and an owner's inability to pay as invalid reasons. An appeal has to show the value exceeds market or is inconsistent with similar properties.

faqs.q: What is the Asheboro city rate on the Randolph County page?
faqs.a: The page prints 0.71 for Asheboro city, plus a school rate of 0.1153. Other towns carry different rates, so match the figure to your parcel.

faqs.q: Who receives the tax bill after a Randolph County sale?
faqs.a: The county says the bill goes to the January 1 owner. How the buyer shares the cost is a closing matter.
